title: Oldest Evidence of Human Cannabis Use Has a Ghoulish Twist - Nautilus
gist: Teaser reporting that archaeologists found cannabis evidence beneath sacrificed-horse burial mounds in southern Siberia, confirming Herodotus' account that the Scythians used cannabis in funeral rites. The visible text does not substantiate the title's 'oldest evidence' claim.

themes.theme: Archaeology confirming Herodotus on the Scythians

insights.claim: Herodotus described a Scythian funerary practice of ritually sacrificing horses, called the 'spectral cavalcade', and archaeologists have confirmed it with burial mounds in southern Siberia topped with sacrificed horse cadavers.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Ancient textual sources can be confirmed selectively by archaeology.
insights.quote: Archaeologists discovered burial mounds in southern Siberia topped with the cadavers of sacrificed horses
insights.locator: Of course, not all of Herodotus

insights.claim: Beneath the spectral cavalcade burials, archaeologists found evidence that the Scythians used cannabis in their funeral rites, as Herodotus had claimed.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Ritual cannabis use has deep historical roots, which is cultural background for cannabis normalization.
insights.quote: The Scythians used cannabis as part of their funeral rites
insights.locator: Of course, not all of Herodotus

insights.claim: Herodotus was not always accurate (he described dog-sized ants that harvested gold), so archaeology is needed to separate his reliable claims from his fanciful ones.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Treat historical narratives as a mix of signal and noise that needs independent verification.
insights.quote: he mentioned dog-sized ants that harvested gold
insights.locator: Of course, not all of Herodotus
